Prepare data for a spax model

Source: R/06-ae_workflow.R, R/08-spax_raster_data.R
prep_data.Rd

Experimental. prep_data() checks and aligns the inputs of a model once, so that model specifications can be bound to them with spax(). It has two modes, chosen by demand.

Usage

prep_data(
  demand,
  supply,
  travel,
  origin_ids = NULL,
  facility_ids = NULL,
  included = NULL,
  missing_demand = c("error", "exclude"),
  missing_travel = c("error", "legacy_zero"),
  spatial = NULL,
  metadata = list(),
  id_col = NULL,
  supply_cols = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'ae_prepared_inputs'
format(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ae_prepared_inputs'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'spax_raster_data'
format(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'spax_raster_data'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

demand

Numeric origin vector, or a named list of them for demand groups (see prepare_allocation()); or a SpatRaster of demand, or a named list of single-layer SpatRasters, one per group. A list that mixes rasters and other elements is an error.

supply

Numeric data: a finite nonnegative facility vector (see prepare_allocation()). Raster data: a data frame with id_col and supply_cols, a matrix or a vector (see spax_e2sfca()); several supply measures give independent layers in an FCA result.

travel

Numeric origin-by-facility travel matrix. It is the distance argument of prepare_allocation(): the same alignment by IDs applies, and with demand groups it can be one matrix shared by the groups or a named list of matrices with one element per group. For raster data, a SpatRaster with one layer per facility (or a named list of them by demand group) on the grid of demand.

origin_ids, facility_ids

Complete unique nonblank canonical IDs. Their order determines prepared order. The default (NULL) takes the names of the demand vector (of the first group for grouped demand) and the column names of the travel matrix; identities are never inferred from equal axis lengths.

included

Nonmissing logical origin mask (default: all TRUE). Names align independently; an unnamed mask follows supplied demand order (that of the first group for grouped demand) and is reordered with demand.

missing_demand

Default "error" rejects included missing demand. "exclude" omits it from loads while recording unknown demand, separately from known zero or explicit exclusion. Positive included demand remains active even when every inside edge is absent.

missing_travel

Default "error" rejects NA/NaN on active fit rows. "legacy_zero" explicitly omits unknown edges and records that policy. Finite nonnegative travel is known, positive infinity is an absent edge, and negative travel is invalid. Omitted rows are validated when requested by prediction. Model-specific finite domains, such as positive power distances, are checked when binding parameters; no imputation bypasses them.

spatial

Optional list with a one-layer terra::SpatRaster template and a complete unique in-range cell_index vector, optionally named by origin ID. Registry positions are not raster cells. Only plain geometry and the aligned mapping are saved. Numeric work needs no spatial metadata.

metadata

Optional named list of scalar strings or NA for demand_units, demand_period, supply_units, supply_period, and travel_units. Omitted fields remain NA. These are caller declarations; no unit conversion or dimensional compatibility check is performed.

id_col, supply_cols

Raster data with a data frame as supply: the column of facility IDs and the character vector of supply columns. They are refused for numeric data.

x

Prepared inputs, an ae_prepared_inputs or spax_raster_data.

...

Unused.

Value

Numeric data: the existing ae_prepared_inputs, as returned by prepare_allocation(). Raster data: a spax_raster_data (also a spax_data), a list with demand and travel (as given), supply (the object as given), id_col, supply_cols, facility_ids (the layer names of the travel stack, or facility_1, ... by position), groups (the group IDs, NULL without groups), metadata (the unit labels) and grid (a list with dim, res and crs of the demand grid). format() returns the printed lines as a character vector and print() returns its argument invisibly.

Details

Numeric data (demand is a numeric vector, or a named list of numeric vectors for demand groups) are the inputs of an allocation model (spec_clm(), spec_huff()): demand by origin, supply by facility and the origin-by-facility travel matrix. In this mode prep_data() is prepare_allocation() under another name, with travel for distance: it returns the identical object, an ae_prepared_inputs, and every argument but id_col and supply_cols is passed through. The step functions (clm_allocation() and the others) accept the object too.

Printing the object lists its origins and facilities, the demand groups, the unit labels when they were given, the active origins whose travel is unknown and the policies for missing demand and travel.

Raster data (demand is a SpatRaster, or a named list of single-layer SpatRasters for demand groups) are the inputs of the floating catchment area indices (spec_e2sfca() and its relatives): demand is the demand grid, travel the travel stack, one layer per facility named by the facility ID, and supply a data frame with id_col and supply_cols, a matrix or a vector, as in spax_e2sfca(). With demand groups, travel can be one stack or a named list of stacks, one per group. prep_data() checks the structure (the demand groups, one geometry, one layer per facility, the supply table) and reads no value of a raster; the demand rule of the indices (finite and nonnegative, NA for unknown) is applied when a model runs. The arguments origin_ids, facility_ids, included, missing_demand, missing_travel and spatial are for numeric data and are refused. id_col and supply_cols are for raster data and are refused for numeric data. The result holds the rasters as they are, so it does not survive saveRDS(): its pointers to the rasters are then empty, and spax() stops and asks for the data to be prepared again.

Allocation models on raster data. spax() also runs spec_clm() and spec_huff() on raster data. It converts the data to origins on each call, behind the scenes, and keeps nothing: the origins are the cells with finite, positive demand (with demand groups, the cells where every group's demand is known and the total is positive), their IDs are the cell numbers of the grid as text ("843"), and the origin registry holds these cells only. The demand rule of the indices applies: negative or infinite demand is an error and NA is unknown. obs_totals() works directly. obs_flows() is keyed by cell number, and counts at cells that are not origins (no demand, or unknown) are dropped with a message. A missing or infinite travel time is an absent pair, and a cell with demand that reaches no facility stays an origin: with spec_clm() its demand goes to the outside option, while spec_huff() has no outside option and allocates none of it. The allocation model uses one supply measure: with several supply_cols, choose one with prep_data(supply_cols = ). The conversion is the same on every call, so fits to the same data share their travel matrix and can be compared with compare_allocations(), and a result does not depend on the rasters after the call.

The travel of the origins is held as a matrix of origins by facilities, 8 bytes per value. On a synthetic grid of 400 x 500 cells with demand in half of them and 250 facilities (100,000 origins), the matrix is 200 MB; converting takes 2 seconds and peaks at about 0.5 GB of R memory (0.85 GB of process memory above the data), 2.5 to 4 times the matrix. A fit to facility totals from one start peaks at about 1.6 GB of R memory (2.6 GB of process memory), about 8 times the matrix, and takes about 2.5 minutes. That is the memory of the fit, the same as for numeric inputs of that size, so a much larger grid is better cropped or coarsened first.

FCA indices on numeric data. An FCA specification (spec_e2sfca() and its relatives) also runs on numeric data with spax(). It gives the index at the active origins only: an origin with zero or unknown demand, or left out, has no row in the result. The result is a spax_access_values (see spax_access_values-methods), not rasters, and numeric data has one supply measure, "supply". A raster sigma (a variable catchment) needs raster data.

See also

Other allocation interface: decay_gaussian(), obs_flows(), spax(), spax_access_values-methods, spax_allocation-methods, spax_huff(), spec_clm()

Examples

# Mainland Cornwall: registered residents, GP FTE and travel minutes
areas <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_lsoa[!cornwall_lsoa$scilly, ])
gp <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_gp[!cornwall_gp$scilly, ])
demand <- stats::setNames(areas$registered, areas$lsoa)
supply <- stats::setNames(gp$gp_fte_extg, gp$practice)
travel <- cornwall_travel[areas$lsoa, gp$practice]
prep_data(demand, supply, travel,
          metadata = list(demand_units = "registered residents",
                          supply_units = "GP FTE", travel_units = "minutes"))
#> <spax data> 336 origins (336 active) x 54 facilities
#>   demand      604,471 registered residents
#>   supply      GP FTE
#>   travel      minutes; unknown for 0 active origins
#>   policies    missing demand: error; missing travel: error

# Raster data for a floating catchment area index
pop <- read_spax_example("cornwall_pop.tif")
travel_grid <- read_spax_example("cornwall_gp_travel.tif")
grid_data <- prep_data(pop, sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_gp), travel_grid,
                       id_col = "practice", supply_cols = "gp_fte_extg")
grid_data
#> <spax data> raster 132 x 271 cells x 55 facilities; supply gp_fte_extg
#>   demand    1 layer; travel 55 layers
#>   note      holds terra rasters: prepare the data again after saveRDS()
spax(grid_data, spec_e2sfca(decay = decay_gaussian(sigma = 10)))
#> <spax access> E2SFCA, 1 layer on 132 x 271 cells
#> 
#> Spatial Properties:
#> - Resolution: 0.00833333 x 0.00833333
#> - Dimensions: 132 x 271
#> 
#> Measures: 1
#> - gp_fte_extg
#> 
#> Facilities: 55
#> 
#> Parameters:
#> - Decay function: gaussian (sigma = 10)
#> - Demand normalization: identity 

# \donttest{
# An allocation model on the mainland grid, fitted to practice totals. Demand
# must count the same people as the totals: residents registered with a GP
# practice. The grid estimates residents in 2020, fewer than the registered
# residents of the mainland small areas, so it is scaled to them and gives
# only where they live.
mainland <- terra::ext(-6, terra::xmax(pop), terra::ymin(pop), terra::ymax(pop))
pop <- terra::crop(pop, mainland)
registered <- pop * sum(areas$registered) /
  terra::global(pop, "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]]
d_mainland <- prep_data(registered, gp,
                        terra::crop(travel_grid[[gp$practice]], mainland),
                        id_col = "practice", supply_cols = "gp_fte_extg")

# Registrations of mainland residents at the mainland practices
flows <- cornwall_flows[cornwall_flows$lsoa %in% areas$lsoa &
                          cornwall_flows$practice %in% gp$practice, ]
totals <- obs_totals(tapply(flows$patients, flows$practice, sum))

# The cells with residents become the origins. The Huff model (power decay,
# fitted attractiveness exponent) is well determined by these totals.
huff <- spax(d_mainland, spec_huff(), observed = totals)
huff
#> <spax allocation> Huff model (no outside option)
#>   decay       power (sigma = exponent): fit
#>   attraction  (kappa * supply)^beta: kappa = 1, beta = fit
#>   outside     none
#>   data        6,912 origins x 54 facilities
#> 
#>   parameter  value   status
#>   sigma      1.059   fitted
#>   beta       0.6123  fitted
#>   v0         0       held
#>   kappa      1       held
#> 
#>   selected    scan1 (start 1 of 3); 3 of 3 starts converged
#>   boundary    none
#>   starts      default search, 15 of 15 grid points, loss poisson

# What the totals say about travel: the fit against no decay
check_fit(huff)
#> <allocation check>
#>     comparator     loss loss_difference contact trip_median trip_p90
#>         fitted -5042045               0       1          11       53
#>       no_decay -5038257            3788       1          40       85
#>  capacity_only -5038282            3763      NA          40       85
#> Trip lengths are one-way, in travel units, weighted by expected flows.
#> 
#> The fitted allocation reproduces the counts better than both comparators.
# }
